hero.title: The Smash alternative
hero.body: Smash lets you send big files, but the free tier can be slow, ad-supported, and everything routes through their cloud. BIShare sends large files through a free browser link — and when the other device is nearby, it skips the upload entirely and transfers straight across, instantly. End-to-end encrypted, no account, free.

why.title: Why switch from Smash?
why.body: Smash is handy for oversized files, but the free plan throttles speed, shows ads, and always uploads to the cloud first — so a file you're handing to someone in the same room still makes a round trip to a server. BIShare gives you a free 10 GB link with no ads, and for nearby transfers it removes the upload completely: the file goes device to device, end-to-end encrypted, as fast as your network allows.

0.b: If the other device is on your network, BIShare beams the file straight across — no cloud round trip, no queue, end-to-end encrypted. There's no size cap, and it works over a hotspot with no internet.

1.b: Share a link, QR code, or 6-character code for files up to 10 GB free. The recipient opens it in any browser and downloads — no app, no account, no ads. Links expire after 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux — send from any platform to any other, or to anyone with just a browser.
